name: KNIFE MILL
desc: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS INNO-KM-200 Knife Mill (Blender) is predominantly used in agriculture, food testing, and forensic laboratories. It is engineered for the rapid size reduction and homogenization of soft, elastic, fibrous, and high-moisture samples like meat, plant leaves, seeds, and chocolate. It features interval, regular, and reverse modes for optimal mixing.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS KNIFE MILL (INNO-KM-200) operates on the principle of high-speed mechanical comminution and homogenization, where razor-sharp stainless steel or titanium-coated blades rotating at 500–10,000 rpm generate intense shear, cutting, impact, and turbulence. This process rapidly reduces soft, elastic, fibrous, and high-moisture matrices into a fine, homogeneous powder or paste with final fineness below 300 μm. The mill supports interval, regular, and reverse modes to optimize sample processing and prevent overheating or clumping. In food testing, agriculture, and forensic laboratories, doctors, B.Sc/M.Sc students, PhD researchers, and chemists routinely use this equipment to prepare samples for downstream analysis such as mycotoxin screening (e.g., aflatoxins in grains), pesticide residue extraction from plant leaves, proximate composition (moisture, fat, protein, fiber) per AOAC/ISO methods, DNA extraction for species identification, and microbiological assays for pathogens like Salmonella, Listeria monocytogenes, and Escherichia coli according to ISO 6887-1 homogenization guidelines. Its electromagnetic safety lid lock ensures safe processing of high-moisture meat, seeds, chocolate, and forensic specimens, making it an essential sample preparation tool in analytical and research workflows.
sop: Ensure the knife mill is placed on a stable, dry bench and the power switch is OFF before connecting to a 220 V, 50 Hz supply.
Open the lid, inspect the stainless steel/titanium blades for damage, and confirm the grinding chamber is clean, dry, and free from residual sample.

Place the pre-weighed sample into the grinding chamber, ensuring the feed size is below 40 mm (or 130 mm for larger model) and the batch volume is within the permitted 150–700 mL (or 1–4.5 L) capacity.
Close the lid securely until the electromagnetic safety lock engages; never bypass or defeat the lid interlock.
Switch on the mains power and select the desired operational mode (interval, reverse, or press-and-play) using the mode selector.
Press the 'SET' button once to enter the controller setting mode.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter (e.g., grinding time 0:01–9:59 min or speed 500–4000/2000–10000 rpm depending on model).
Press 'SET' again to lock the value and store the set point.
Press the start/run button to begin the grinding cycle; monitor the process until the preset time elapses and the rotor comes to a complete stop.
After the cycle stops, open the lid only after the blades have fully stopped, collect the homogenized sample with a clean spatula, and immediately clean the chamber and blades.

SAFETY WARNING: Always disconnect the power plug before cleaning or blade removal; blades are extremely sharp and can cause severe laceration. Wear cut-resistant gloves and safety glasses, and never process flammable solvents, hard/brittle materials, or operate the mill with the lid open or interlock bypassed.
features: Razor-sharp blades (Stainless Steel or Titanium coating/alloy)
High-speed motor adjustable from 500 up to 10000 rpm (Model dependent)
Coarse grinding and fine grinding realized in one step
Electromagnetic safety lid lock prevents opening during grinding
Supports dry as well as wet grinding applications

specifications.Operational Modes: Interval mode, Reverse mode, Press-and-play mode
specifications.Target Applications: Food Testing, Agriculture, Forensics, Meat & Plant Homogenization
